graham.brief:
Of everything posted for this game, TreVeyon Henderson at 10.5 rush attempts is the line worth stopping on. Henderson is at 12 rush attempts a game across two games so far. The books look for about 21 points from New England, with a 48.5 total on the game. So why is Henderson priced below his own season?

Henderson's own last game is a good place to start. Henderson's volume fell from 16 to 9 last week. If New England keeps trimming his work, the early games describe a bigger job than he has now. As the underdog, New England could be throwing more once the fourth quarter arrives.

Some of the New England evidence cuts the other way. Buffalo's run defense gives up ground, 7th-worst in the league at stopping the run.

That's the open Henderson question. One reading points to his recent workload, the other to a two-game baseline for Henderson that's still noisy. Two games of Henderson can point somewhere without proving anything.

Count the New England handoffs in the first quarter, since Henderson's share shows up early or it doesn't.
